extracted.intended_audience: marketing and PR professionals (marketers, PR teams, small business founders) writing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating effective press releases: the required structural elements, writing/style rules, multimedia and distribution tactics to increase pickup and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a media contact section either at the top or bottom of the release so journalists can follow up. (Page states placement only; specific fields not enumerated.)

rubrics_metrics.name: "For immediate release" notice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark the release timing clearly (e.g., "For immediate release") in the indicated position so recipients know the distribution timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline format
rubrics_metrics.description: Dateline (city and state in all caps + release date)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a dateline that lists the city and state in all caps followed by the release date to situate the story geographically and temporally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, explanatory headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline that quickly explains the announcement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a headline that immediately communicates the news; later guidance emphasizes making headlines interesting and SEO-aware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business location in lead
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the company location in the first sentence to reinforce the dateline and local relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate at end
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude with a brief company bio (boilerplate) describing the organization; this should appear at the end of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: End signifier
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a conventional signifier (e.g., "###") to mark the end of the release for editors and wire services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsy, straightforward writing style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a news-style tone rather than promotional copy; write plainly and directly so the release reads like a news article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame as a news article
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagine it as an article on a news site
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose the release so it could be republished as a standalone news article — focus on newsworthiness and objective presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong first paragraph (lead)
rubrics_metrics.description: First paragraph: state announcement + business context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the core announcement and provide the relevant business context immediately (who, what, when, where, why/how). The page emphasizes the first paragraph should clearly state the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AP style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Associated Press (AP) style conventions for punctuation, numbers, titles, and general journalistic consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focused paragraphing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break the release into several short paragraphs, each dedicated to a single idea or fact to aid readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose template appropriate to announcement type
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates for product release, event announcement, partnership/acquisition, funding announcement, new hire/promotion, award announcement, survey/research findings, crisis response
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the template that matches the announcement (HubSpot provides templates for common types). Tailor content to the chosen template's expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan keywords (SEO)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategically incorporate keywords to help discoverability and SEO; HubSpot highlights planning keywords as a key writing tip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write interesting headlines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond explaining the announcement, craft headlines that capture attention and encourage clicks or pickup by journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multimedia and quotes to vary content
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary content with multimedia and quotes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quotes and different media formats to make the story richer and more usable for editors and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include photos
rubrics_metrics.description: Photos are #1 factor positively influencing views and engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach high-quality photos; HubSpot reports photos as the single biggest positive influence on views and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell a story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the announcement as a narrative where appropriate to increase interest and context rather than a list of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multimedia to boost engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed or attach multimedia (photos, infographics, video, b-roll) as it generally increases engagement and usability for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution via wire service for major news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a wire service when the announcement has broad, national, or major news value to maximize reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct pitching to relevant journalists
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and pitch the journalists and outlets most likely to cover the story for targeted pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post on company newsroom
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish the release on the company's own newsroom or press page so it’s discoverable and shareable directly from the brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share on social media
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage social channels to amplify the release and reach audiences and reporters who follow the brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch industry publications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target industry- or trade-specific publications for better topical fit and likely coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infographics for data stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include infographics when presenting survey or research findings to make data more digestible and compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Videos for product launches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use product demo videos or other video content to illustrate product launches and increase engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: B-roll for broadcast use
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide B-roll footage when the story may be covered by TV or video-producing outlets to facilitate broadcast use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include headshots for executive quotes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach headshots to accompany executive or spokesperson quotes so outlets can pair images with bylines or captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of required elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the release contains all the basic structural elements (contact info, dateline, headline, lead, boilerplate, end signifier) to be considered complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-promotional, newsy tone
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overt marketing language; the page emphasizes framing the release as newsworthy rather than promotional advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear announcement in first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release should make the central news clear immediately in the opening paragraph to maximize journalist and reader comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include location/context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide geographic and situational context (dateline, business location, relevant background) so the news is properly situated for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic keyword placement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place SEO keywords thoughtfully in headline and lead to improve searchability while maintaining natural journalistic tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginable as a news article
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the release can be read as a standalone news article without heavy promotional framing, it meets HubSpot's standard for good press releases.
